official.deadline_note: The Foundation publishes one fixed annual window: the portal opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March. The 2026 window ran 1 January to 1 March 2026 and the 2026 cohort was announced on 22 March 2026, so the next opportunity to apply is the window opening 1 January 2027. The Foundation has not yet published a separate 2027 announcement.
official.application_cycle: Annual cohort cycle. 2026 applications ran 1 January to 1 March 2026; the standing published rule is a 1 January to midnight 1 March window each year, so the next window is 1 January to 1 March 2027.
official.status_note: The 2026 application window (1 January to midnight 1 March 2026) has closed and the 3,200-strong 2026 cohort was announced on 22 March 2026, selected from over 265,000 applications with the assessment conducted by Ernst & Young. The Foundation publishes no 2027 window announcement; its programme page states the portal opens on 1 January every year.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition payment is published. The Foundation describes the award as non-returnable seed capital for a business, not a scholarship, so no tuition or living costs are paid.

Financial understanding, weighted 10%: basic understanding of revenue streams, cost drivers and financing needs, with realistic financial forecasts
Scalability, weighted 30%: potential to replicate the model across community, regional, national and continental markets
Leadership and entrepreneurial skills, weighted 15%: passion and commitment, previous accomplishments mobilising people and resources, and experience and technical expertise

official.description: Launched in 2015, the TEF Entrepreneurship Programme is the Foundation's flagship annual initiative for African entrepreneurs, delivered on its TEFConnect digital platform. It combines business management training, mentorship and coaching with a USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital award for selected participants whose businesses are judged investment-ready. The Foundation states the programme has provided training to 2.5 million Africans and disbursed over US$100 million to more than 24,000 entrepreneurs, creating over 1.5 million direct and indirect jobs.
official.program_type: Foundation entrepreneurship grant and training programme

applicant_utility.summary: This is a business grant, not a degree scholarship: USD 5,000 of non-refundable seed capital paid into a registered business account, wrapped around TEF's online business management training, mentorship and alumni network. The only way in is a single two-month window on TEFConnect that opens every 1 January and shuts at midnight on 1 March, and you cannot be a past TEF beneficiary. Everything downstream - business registration, tax registration, a bank reference letter, a business plan and a pitch video - must be in place before any money moves, so the real work starts months before the portal opens.
applicant_utility.best_fit: An African aged 18 or over living in Africa with a business idea, or a business under five years old, that can create jobs and plausibly scale beyond its home market.
application_readiness_checklist: Before the window opens, have a colour scan of your government ID that shows date of birth and photo, and a high-resolution headshot, ready to upload.
Type your name into TEFConnect exactly as it appears on that ID - a single spelling mismatch is an avoidable, fatal discrepancy.
Practise aptitude-style business tests and sharpen your unit economics, because the application contains a scored business assessment test and a minimum score is required to be deemed eligible.

Draft the business properly first: target market and segments, pricing, competitors, revenue model, cost lines and break-even, since feasibility, market opportunity, financial understanding, scalability and leadership all carry shortlist weight.
Budget for business registration, notarisation, tax registration and a business bank account, since seed capital is only paid into a business account.
Block out the calendar around the 1 March closure, the 22 March shortlist notification and the onboarding session, then the training and investment-readiness deadlines that follow.
common_rejection_risks: Scoring below the minimum in the application business assessment test - you are notified as ineligible on the spot and encouraged to reapply the following year.
A name or personal-details mismatch between your TEFConnect profile and your government-issued ID.
A business older than five years, or a business you intend to run from outside Africa, both of which breach published eligibility rules.
Having previously benefitted from any TEF programme, or applying twice in the same application window of the same year.
Documents found to be inauthentic, containing discrepancies, or matching the document details of past TEF Entrepreneurship Programme beneficiaries - these lead to immediate disqualification.
An incoherent or information-thin business description; the Foundation's own lowest score band describes applications where key fields were left blank and the idea could not be understood.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: All of your living costs throughout the cycle, plus business registration and notarisation, tax registration, business bank account opening, travel to any physical verification or onboarding session, and any capital the business needs beyond the USD 5,000 award.
document_audit: The ID must show date of birth and photo and must match TEFConnect exactly; only a National Driver's Licence, an International Passport or a Permanent Voter's Card (Nigerian participants only) is accepted.
Tax registration and the bank reference letter must both be in the business name, and the bank letter must carry your name, the business name and the business bank details.
A Partner Consent form is needed only if you are a co-owner of the business, and a hospital medical report only if you are living with a disability.
The headshot must be high resolution - poor-quality uploads are a common and entirely avoidable failure.
The business plan, financial projection and pitch video are reviewed by an independent audit consulting firm and ranked, so treat them as investment documents rather than coursework.
alerts: The window is two months long and does not roll: miss midnight on 1 March and your next attempt is a full year away.
Do not trust aggregator deadlines - several list a 31 March closing date, which contradicts the Foundation's own published midnight 1 March close.

Seed capital is released only after 100% completion of the training modules, submission of the business plan, financial projection and a 2-3 minute pitch video, and signing the seed capital undertaking.

Shortlisted applicants undergo LSEG World-Check screening and physical or virtual verification, and documents are re-reviewed by the TEF Audit and Finance team, so allow time for at least one resubmission round.
Ernst & Young has anchored the selection process since 2023, and EY quality assurance experts validate results before the final selection.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply on TEFConnect during the 1 January to 1 March window, pass the automatic eligibility screen and assessment-test threshold, then survive EY-led review, World-Check screening and physical verification before the 22 March shortlist is notified.

official.deadline_central_display: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time.
official.deadline_note: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme; applications can be submitted at any time. The current open round opened on 25 August 2026. Assessment is not instantaneous: shortlisting panels meet three times a year (February, June and September) and interviews three times a year (May, September and January), so a February shortlist means a May interview.
official.application_cycle: Rolling with three assessment rounds a year. Open round: applications opened 25 August 2026, no deadline. Shortlisting three times a year (February, June, September); interviews three times a year (May, September, January).
official.status_note: The scheme page lists an open round with applications opening 25 August 2026 and no deadline, inviting applications at any time. A July 2026 round closed to new applications with a deadline of 21 July 2026, 15:00 BST, with shortlisting in October 2026 and interviews on 12-14 January 2027. Wellcome states it does not accept late applications.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award funds the total cost of the grantholder's salary plus research expenses. It is a research grant administered by an organisation, not a studentship: Wellcome states explicitly that no studentships are provided on this award.
official.funding_period: up to, for research expenses over the award
benefits: The total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire period of the grant, determined by the administering organisation, including basic salary, employer contributions, pension scheme costs, incremental salary progression and locally recognised allowances
Up to £400,000 for research expenses, with overheads, overseas allowances, adjustment support and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques sitting outside that limit
Staff salary costs, full or part-time, up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post

Relocation allowance of up to £1,000 to cover personal removal costs, plus visa and work permit costs for the grantholder, their partner and dependent children and Immigration Health Surcharge costs where relevant

If, after two or more years from the award activation date, the organisation awards a permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract that includes the salary, the grantholder keeps the salary element of the award for remaining research costs
Award holders who need a visa to work in the UK may be eligible for a Global Talent Visa, and the award can be held part-time with the duration extended
eligibility: Ability to conduct independent, original research that makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge, demonstrated either by a passed PhD or equivalent higher research degree thesis defence by the date you submit your application, or by at least four years' research experience equivalent to a PhD; research undertaken during undergraduate or Master's degrees does not count towards the experience route

No more than three years of postdoctoral experience in the proposed field at the date of submission, unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted on your research career, with allowances for part-time work, career breaks and time spent outside research
At least 80% of research time contributed to the project, with no more than 20% of time on non-research activities, or up to 40% on clinical duties for clinical craft specialties

Administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China, and must be not-for-profit (higher education institution, research institute or healthcare organisation)

A sponsor at the administering organisation holding an established post, or an honorary academic appointment, for the duration of the award who guarantees the space and resources, plus a mentor with a track record in training and mentorship (the sponsor can also be the mentor; neither is paid for their input)

Not eligible if you have an existing tenured salaried post for the duration of the award unless based in a low- or middle-income country, or if you hold, have held or have accepted an offer for an equivalent award at this career stage; coapplicants are not accepted and you may only have one application under consideration as lead applicant across the Early Career Award, Career Development Award and Discovery Award schemes
requirements: Submit your application through Wellcome Funding, and only once all required sections and documents are complete
Check your eligibility using Wellcome's self-assessment tool; Wellcome notes applications are often withdrawn because the researcher does not meet eligibility requirements
Check that your type of research project is within what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research before applying

Obtain a sponsor statement from an individual at your administering organisation who holds an established post for the duration of the award, and identify a mentor with a track record in training and mentorship
If requesting overheads, provide a letter from your Finance Director stating how overhead costs were calculated, including confirmation of any externally validated rate and when it was last reviewed
Cost the application at 1.0 (100%) full-time equivalent even if you intend to hold the award on a part-time basis, with the duration extended later to reflect this
documents: Research proposal and budget costed in the Wellcome Funding system
Sponsor statement from an individual at the administering organisation holding an established post for the duration of the award
Mentor details, which may be the same person as the sponsor
Letter of support from the director of finance at the administering organisation, if overheads are requested
Letter of support from the person overseeing your clinical training, if you intend to complete clinical training during the award
selection_criteria: Your research proposal, weighted 50% at interview stage: bold, creative and high quality, well-designed, clear, supported by evidence, with feasible outcomes and outputs
Your skills and experience, weighted 25%: previous research outputs and contributions to the research community
Your research environment, weighted 25%: how your research environment or environments will support you to deliver your research programme and develop as a researcher
coverage: Basic salary determined by the administering organisation, including employer's contributions, pension scheme costs, incremental progression and locally recognised allowances such as London allowance
Up to £400,000 for research expenses, with additional staff salary costs up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post
Materials and consumables, animals, equipment purchase and maintenance, computer equipment, and access charges for shared equipment, facilities or services
Travel and subsistence for collaborative visits and other essential visits, plus conference attendance of £2,000 a year for the grantholder and £1,000 each a year for research and technical staff
Visa and work permit costs for the grantholder, partner and dependent children, Immigration Health Surcharge costs, and a relocation allowance of up to £1,000 for personal removal costs
Continuing professional development and professional skills training up to £500 a year per person, and research skills training, for staff in posts of 12 months or more working at 50% FTE or more
application_method: Check your eligibility using Wellcome's self-assessment tool and confirm your research fits what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research
Agree your administering organisation and secure a sponsor and a mentor
Prepare the research proposal and budget, costing salaries on your organisation's pay scales
Complete the application form on Wellcome Funding and submit it to the approver at your administering organisation for approval
The administering organisation approves and submits the application to Wellcome

Applications are shortlisted by Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups, then external written expert review is sought on shortlisted applications; shortlisted candidates are interviewed by the Early-Career Interview Committee at the Wellcome offices in London, including a presentation, and final funding decisions are made by the Discovery Research Decision Board
official.application_route: Apply on the Wellcome Funding platform (funding.wellcome.org); your administering organisation's approver approves and submits the final application to Wellcome.
official.study_mode: Full-time. The award may be held on a part-time basis with the duration extended to reflect this, but the application must be costed at 1.0 (100%) full-time equivalent.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality or citizenship rule is published for this scheme. Eligibility is location-based: the lead applicant's administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China. From 29 October 2026 only administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia are eligible.
official.international_eligibility: There is no published nationality restriction; international applicants are eligible provided the lead applicant's administering organisation meets the location rules and the other eligibility criteria are met.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any discipline is eligible, including STEM, experimental medicine, humanities and social science, clinical/allied health sciences and public health, provided the research fits within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and has the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing. There is no agency restriction.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal that fits within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and has the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing, or that develops methodologies, conceptual frameworks, tools or techniques that could benefit health-related research. The proposal must not fall outside the Discovery Research remit, and applicants must check this before applying.
official.duration: Usually 5 years, but may be less for some disciplines such as humanities and social science, and may only be longer if held on a part-time basis
official.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award funds early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and, through innovative projects, deliver shifts in understanding related to human life, health and wellbeing. It provides the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire grant period plus up to £400,000 for research expenses, over an award that usually lasts five years. By the end of the award the grantholder should be ready to lead their own independent research programme.
official.region: UK, Republic of Ireland and low- and middle-income countries, changing from 29 October 2026 to the UK plus low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia
official.program_type: Charitable foundation research grant (no studentships provided)

not_confirmed: english_requirement (no English language proficiency requirement is published; English language tests appear only as a reimbursable visa-related cost)
funding_amount as a single total, because the £400,000 is a cap on research expenses and the grantholder's salary is funded separately at the full cost
tuition_coverage and living_cost_coverage, because the award pays salary and research costs rather than tuition or living costs
verification.notes: The £400,000 research expenses limit, the salary arrangement, the five-year duration, the no-deadline rolling application, the assessment weightings, the open round opening on 25 August 2026, the three shortlisting and interview rounds a year, and the 29 October 2026 location eligibility change were all read directly on Wellcome's own scheme page and eligibility self-assessment page. Overheads, conference, relocation and training limits were taken from the research costs section of the same page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a five-year research grant for someone who has just finished a PhD and wants to run their own programme: Wellcome pays your salary in full and gives you up to £400,000 for research costs, with no application deadline. It is a grant to an organisation rather than a studentship, so you need a host institution in an eligible country, a sponsor there, and a proposal that sits squarely inside Discovery Research. The two things that sink most applications are career-stage eligibility and a proposal whose link to human health is not explicit.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A researcher within three years of their viva, with a sponsor and host in the UK, Ireland or an eligible LMIC, and a distinct health-linked research idea they can lead independently.
application_readiness_checklist: Run Wellcome's five-minute self-assessment tool first; Wellcome states that applications are often withdrawn before shortlisting because the researcher is ineligible.
Read the Discovery Research remit page and state your proposal's health relevance explicitly - Wellcome identifies proposals not sufficiently related to human health as the main withdrawal reason.

Secure a sponsor at your administering organisation who holds an established post for the duration of the award and will guarantee space and resources, and identify a mentor (your sponsor can be both).
Cost salaries on your host organisation's pay scales, including employer contributions and pension, and build the budget inside the Wellcome Funding system rather than in a spreadsheet.
Ask your Finance Director early for the overhead letter if you want overheads, and keep total overhead cost under 20% of direct research costs.
Confirm you have no other live lead application on the Early Career, Career Development or Discovery Award schemes, and hold no equivalent award at this career stage.
common_rejection_risks: Withdrawal before shortlisting because the lead applicant falls outside the career-stage window - more than three years of postdoctoral experience, or a viva not yet passed at submission.
Withdrawal because the proposal does not fit what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research, most often because the connection to human health is not made explicit.
Applying from an administering organisation that fails the location rules; from 29 October 2026 that excludes Republic of Ireland and Latin American organisations.
Scoring in the lowest levels at shortlisting, which removes the right to resubmit that project at all.
Holding, or having accepted an offer for, an equivalent award at this career stage, or an existing tenured salaried post unless based in a low- or middle-income country.
Intending to carry out activities that involve transferring grant funds into mainland China, which is explicitly prohibited.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything outside the grant conditions: core infrastructure your host organisation should provide, studentships, potential promotion costs on your salary, capital or building works for access adjustments such as ramps, business-class flights, and non-justified additional overheads on top of the 20% cap.
document_audit: There is no CV or publication list upload on this scheme - the application form questions carry the evidence, so your outputs and track record have to be written into the form itself.
Only two attachments are called for: a clinical-training support letter if you will complete clinical training during the award, and a Finance Director letter if you are requesting overheads.
Your administering organisation must have a Wellcome Funding account and an approver, because the organisation submits the final application, not you.
If you plan to work more than three months away from your administering organisation, you need an additional sponsor at that location guaranteeing space and resources for the visit.
Cost the application at 1.0 full-time equivalent even if you intend to hold the award part-time; the duration is extended later to reflect this.
alerts: Location eligibility tightens on 29 October 2026: applications submitted on or before 28 October 2026 are assessed under the current rules, after which only UK and LMIC organisations in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia qualify.

It is rolling but not fast: shortlisting runs in February, June and September with interviews in May, September and January, so a decision realistically takes months and planning should allow for that.
You can only hold one of these awards and Wellcome does not offer renewals.

Resubmission is capped: the same project may be considered a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed calls, and a lowest-band shortlist score ends that project's chances entirely.
No studentships are provided on this award, so do not budget for PhD students on it.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the form on Wellcome Funding, your administering organisation's approver approves and submits it, then shortlisting by Advisory Groups, external written expert review, an interview with the Early-Career Interview Committee in London, and a final decision by the Discovery Research Decision Board.
